questions.question: Explain, using ideas about disorder, whether the sign of your answer to (a)(i) is as expected for the Haber process.
questions.answer: The entropy change of the system is negative, as expected, because 4 mol of gas form 2 mol of gas, so disorder decreases
steps: Haber reaction: N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g).
Reactants contain 1 + 3 = 4 mol of gas; products contain 2 mol of gas.
Fewer gas molecules means fewer ways to arrange them, so the disorder decreases.
So the entropy change of the system is negative, as expected.

questions.topic: Entropy Change Of Surroundings At 700 K
questions.question: At 700 K the enthalpy change for the Haber reaction is -110.2 kJ mol-1. Calculate the entropy change of the surroundings at 700 K, including sign and units.
steps: deltaS(surr) = -deltaH / T.
deltaH = -110.2 kJ mol-1 = -110 200 J mol-1.
The sign is positive because the reaction is exothermic and releases heat to the surroundings.

questions.topic: Entropy Change Of System From Total
questions.question: At 700 K the total entropy change is -78.7 J K-1 mol-1. Using your answer to (a)(iii), calculate the entropy change of the system, including sign and units.
steps: deltaStotal = deltaSsystem + deltaSsurroundings.
deltaSsystem = deltaStotal - deltaSsurroundings = -78.7 - 157.4.
deltaSsystem = -236.1 J K-1 mol-1.

questions.topic: Advantage And Disadvantage Of Higher Temperature
questions.question: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using a temperature higher than 700 K in the Haber process, considering the rate of reaction, the values of deltaSsurroundings and deltaStotal, and the equilibrium constant.
questions.answer: Advantage: faster rate. Disadvantage: the exothermic reaction gives a lower equilibrium constant and yield, and deltaSsurroundings and deltaStotal both fall
steps: Advantage: raising the temperature increases the kinetic energy of the molecules, so more collisions have energy above Ea and the rate increases.
Disadvantage: the forward reaction is exothermic, so higher temperature shifts equilibrium to the left and lowers the equilibrium constant and yield of ammonia.
deltaSsurroundings = -deltaH / T, so it decreases as T rises (less positive).
deltaStotal = deltaSsystem + deltaSsurroundings, so it becomes less positive (more negative) at higher T, making the reaction less feasible.
Overall the trade-off is between a faster rate and a lower yield and lower feasibility.

questions.question: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant Kp for the Haber process, N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g).
steps: Products go on the top, reactants on the bottom, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient.
Ammonia (product) has coefficient 2, so it appears as p(NH3)^2.
Nitrogen has coefficient 1 and hydrogen has coefficient 3, so the denominator is p(N2) x p(H2)^3.

questions.question: A mixture of N2, H2 and NH3 is at equilibrium at 255 atm and 700 K. The partial pressure of N2 is 25 atm and of H2 is 150 atm. Calculate Kp at 700 K, including units.
steps: Partial pressure of NH3 = total pressure - p(N2) - p(H2) = 255 - 25 - 150 = 80 atm.
Denominator = 25 x 3 375 000 = 84 375 000 atm^4.

questions.topic: Effect Of Pressure Doubling On Yield
questions.question: The pressure of the Haber system is doubled at constant temperature. Explain the effect on the yield of ammonia by considering the change in Kp and the position of equilibrium.
questions.answer: Kp is unchanged because it depends only on temperature; the equilibrium shifts to the right (fewer gas moles), so the ammonia yield increases
steps: Kp depends only on temperature, so doubling the pressure at constant T does not change Kp.
Doubling all partial pressures changes Q = p(NH3)^2 / (p(N2) p(H2)^3) to a value 2^2 / 2^4 = 1/4 of its equilibrium value, so Q falls below Kp.
Gas moles fall from 4 (left) to 2 (right), so the system responds by shifting to the side with fewer gas molecules, which is to the right.
So the position of equilibrium moves to the right and the yield of ammonia increases.

steps: Kc = 4.85 is greater than 1, so the position of equilibrium lies towards the products (Y and Z).
All four species are still present, because the equilibrium is not complete (Kc is not very large).
So the mixture contains more Y and Z than W and X, which is option D.

questions.topic: Lattice Energy Agreement For CaF2 And CaI2
questions.question: Explain why the Born-Haber and theoretical lattice energies are similar for calcium fluoride but significantly different for calcium iodide.
questions.answer: Fluoride is small and not very polarisable, so CaF2 is nearly ionic; iodide is large and very polarisable, so CaI2 has much covalent character not in the ionic model
steps: The theoretical lattice energy assumes purely ionic bonding with point charges.
The F- ion is small and hard to polarise, so the bonding in CaF2 is close to ionic and the two values agree.
The I- ion is large with a diffuse electron cloud, so it is easily polarised by Ca2+.
This polarisation gives CaI2 significant covalent character, so its Born-Haber value differs greatly from the ionic theoretical value.

questions.topic: Electron Affinity Of Chlorine Versus Iodine
questions.question: The electron affinity of iodine is -295.4 kJ mol-1. Explain how the electron affinity of chlorine differs from that of iodine.
questions.answer: Chlorine has a more exothermic (more negative) electron affinity because it is smaller, so the added electron is closer to the nucleus and feels a stronger attraction
steps: Electron affinity is the energy change when an electron is added to a gaseous atom.
Chlorine is smaller than iodine, so the outer electron shell is closer to the nucleus.
The incoming electron experiences a stronger attraction to the nucleus in Cl than in I.
There is also less shielding and less repulsion from the existing electrons, so chlorine releases more energy and has a more exothermic electron affinity than iodine.

questions.question: The reversible reaction between hydrogen chloride and oxygen gives water vapour and chlorine. Explain the effect of an increase in total pressure on the yield of chlorine and on Kp.
questions.answer: Yield of chlorine increases because the equilibrium shifts to the side with fewer gas moles; Kp is unchanged because temperature is constant
steps: The equation is 4HCl(g) + O2(g) <=> 2H2O(g) + 2Cl2(g).
Left side has 5 mol of gas; right side has 4 mol of gas.
Increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles, which is the right-hand side.
So more chlorine is formed and the yield of chlorine increases.
Kp depends only on temperature, so Kp is unchanged.

questions.question: Explain the effect of an increase in temperature on the yield of chlorine at equilibrium and on Kp for the reaction between hydrogen chloride and oxygen.
questions.answer: The yield of chlorine decreases and Kp decreases, because the forward reaction is exothermic
steps: The forward reaction (4HCl + O2 -> 2H2O + 2Cl2) is exothermic.
Increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium in the endothermic direction, which is to the left.
So the yield of chlorine decreases.
Kp falls because the equilibrium constant of an exothermic reaction decreases as temperature rises.

questions.question: Explain the effect of using a catalyst on the yield of chlorine at equilibrium and on Kp.
questions.answer: A catalyst has no effect on the yield or on Kp; it only increases the rate at which equilibrium is reached
steps: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for both the forward and reverse reactions equally.
So it increases the rate at which equilibrium is reached.
It does not change the position of equilibrium, so the yield of chlorine is unchanged.
Kp depends only on temperature, so Kp is unchanged.

questions.topic: Kp Expression For HCl And O2 Equilibrium
questions.question: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant Kp for 4HCl(g) + O2(g) <=> 2H2O(g) + 2Cl2(g).
questions.answer: Kp = p(H2O)^2 x p(Cl2)^2 / (p(HCl)^4 x p(O2))
steps: Products on the top: H2O with coefficient 2 and Cl2 with coefficient 2.
Reactants on the bottom: HCl with coefficient 4 and O2 with coefficient 1.
So Kp = p(H2O)^2 p(Cl2)^2 / (p(HCl)^4 p(O2)).

questions.topic: Kc Expression For Water Gas Reaction
questions.question: For the water gas reaction C(s) + H2O(g) <=> CO(g) + H2(g), deltaH = +131.2 kJ mol-1, what is the equilibrium constant Kc?
questions.answer: Kc = [CO][H2] / [H2O] (carbon is a solid and is left out)
steps: Solids are not included in equilibrium expressions.
Products CO and H2 go on the top, and the gas reactant H2O goes on the bottom.
So Kc = [CO][H2] / [H2O].

questions.topic: Effect Of Temperature On Forward And Reverse K
questions.question: What happens to the equilibrium constants of the forward and reverse reactions when the temperature is increased for the endothermic water gas reaction?
questions.answer: The forward equilibrium constant increases and the reverse equilibrium constant decreases
steps: The forward reaction is endothermic (deltaH = +131.2 kJ mol-1).
Increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction, so the forward K increases.
The reverse reaction is exothermic, so its K decreases as temperature rises.

questions.question: Give the expression for the equilibrium constant Kp for the hydration of ethene, C2H4(g) + H2O(g) <=> C2H5OH(g).
questions.answer: Kp = p(C2H5OH) / (p(C2H4) x p(H2O))
steps: The equation is C2H4(g) + H2O(g) <=> C2H5OH(g).
Ethanol (product) goes on the top, and ethene and steam (reactants) go on the bottom.
Kp = p(C2H5OH) / (p(C2H4) x p(H2O)).

questions.question: 1.00 mol ethene and 1.00 mol steam are mixed at 150 C. At equilibrium the total pressure is 50.0 atm and 0.450 mol ethanol has formed. Calculate Kp for the hydration of ethene, including units.
steps: Equilibrium moles: ethene = 1.00 - 0.450 = 0.550; steam = 1.00 - 0.450 = 0.550; ethanol = 0.450; total = 1.550 mol.
Partial pressure = (mol / total mol) x 50.0 atm: p(C2H4) = p(H2O) = 0.550/1.550 x 50.0 = 17.7 atm.
Units: atm / (atm x atm) = atm^-1, so Kp = 0.0461 atm^-1.

questions.question: The industrial manufacture of ethanol is at 230 C and 70 atm, with an overall conversion of 95%. Comment on these conditions in relation to their effect on the equilibrium and the overall yield of ethanol.
questions.answer: High pressure favours ethanol (fewer gas moles), a high temperature lowers the equilibrium yield (exothermic) but speeds the rate, and the 95% overall yield is achieved by recycling unreacted ethene
steps: Hydration of ethene is exothermic, so a high temperature shifts the equilibrium to the left and lowers the equilibrium yield.
The temperature of 230 C is a compromise, giving a reasonable rate while keeping the equilibrium yield acceptable.
There are 2 mol of gas on the left and 1 mol on the right, so the high pressure of 70 atm shifts equilibrium to the right and increases the yield.
The overall conversion of 95% is higher than the single-pass equilibrium yield, because unreacted ethene and steam are recycled.

questions.topic: Effect Of Lowering Temperature On Equilibrium
questions.question: For C(s) + CO2(g) <=> 2CO(g), where the forward reaction is endothermic, which will increase when the temperature is lowered? Options: A the mole fraction of carbon dioxide, B the partial pressure of carbon monoxide, C the rate of the backward reaction, D the value of Kp for the forward reaction.
questions.answer: A - the mole fraction of carbon dioxide
steps: Forward reaction is endothermic, so lowering the temperature shifts equilibrium to the left (exothermic direction).
The reactant CO2 increases in amount, so its mole fraction increases: option A.
CO partial pressure falls, the rate of the backward reaction falls, and Kp falls, so B, C and D are wrong.

steps: Mole fraction of CO2 = 1 - 0.526 = 0.474 (only CO and CO2 are present).
Partial pressure = mole fraction x total pressure = 0.474 x 1 atm = 0.474 atm.
This matches option C.

questions.question: For Pb2+(aq) + 2Cl-(aq) <=> PbCl2(s), what are the units of Kc? Options: A dm9 mol-3, B dm6 mol-2, C mol2 dm-6, D mol3 dm-9.
questions.answer: A - dm9 mol-3
steps: PbCl2 is a solid, so it is left out: Kc = 1 / ([Pb2+][Cl-]^2).
Units of [Pb2+][Cl-]^2 = mol dm-3 x (mol dm-3)^2 = mol3 dm-9.
Kc units = 1 / (mol3 dm-9) = dm9 mol-3, which is option A.

questions.question: For 4NH3(g) + 5O2(g) <=> 4NO(g) + 6H2O(g), deltaH = -905 kJ mol-1, which conditions give the greatest equilibrium yield of NO? Options: A high T and high P, B high T and low P, C low T and high P, D low T and low P.
questions.answer: D - low temperature and low pressure
steps: The forward reaction is exothermic, so a low temperature shifts equilibrium to the right, increasing NO yield.
Gas moles increase from 9 (left) to 10 (right), so a low pressure shifts equilibrium to the right.
So low temperature and low pressure give the greatest equilibrium yield, option D.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why only a small amount of energy is required to maintain the nitric acid process? Options: A the catalyst increases the equilibrium yield of NO, B the catalyst decreases the activation energy, C the reaction is thermodynamically feasible, D the reaction is highly exothermic.
questions.answer: D - the reaction is highly exothermic
steps: The reaction releases a large amount of heat (deltaH = -905 kJ mol-1).
This released heat keeps the process at high temperature once started, so little extra energy is needed.
A catalyst only changes the rate, not the energy balance, so A and B are not the reason.
So option D is the best explanation.

questions.question: The total pressure is doubled to 8.0 atm. State the effect on Kp.
questions.answer: Kp is unchanged, because it depends only on temperature
steps: Kp is an equilibrium constant, which depends only on temperature.
Temperature is constant here, so Kp does not change when the pressure is doubled.
Only a change in temperature alters the value of Kp, so the answer is that Kp is unchanged.

questions.topic: Effect Of Pressure On Percentage Dissociation
questions.question: The total pressure is doubled to 8.0 atm at constant temperature. Explain the change in the percentage dissociation of N2O4 by considering the effect on the partial pressures of NO2 and N2O4.
questions.answer: The percentage dissociation decreases: doubling pressure shifts the equilibrium towards N2O4 (fewer gas moles), so less N2O4 dissociates
steps: N2O4 <=> 2NO2: the right side has 2 mol of gas and the left has 1 mol.
Doubling the pressure shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles, which is N2O4.
So the partial pressure of N2O4 rises more than NO2 and the percentage dissociation falls.
Kp is unchanged, so the ratio p(NO2)^2 / p(N2O4) stays the same, which forces the composition to shift towards N2O4.

questions.question: Which statement describes what is happening at equilibrium between iodine in water and iodine in trichloromethane? Options: A iodine molecules move from water to trichloromethane only, B iodine molecules move from trichloromethane to water only, C iodine molecules move both ways, D there is no movement of individual iodine molecules.
questions.answer: C - iodine molecules move from water to trichloromethane and from trichloromethane to water at equal rates
steps: At equilibrium the system is dynamic: molecules keep moving in both directions.
The forward and reverse rates of transfer between the two layers are equal.
So the overall concentrations stay constant while molecules continue to move, which is option C.

questions.topic: Increasing Kc For Calcium Carbonate Decomposition
questions.question: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant for heating limestone (CaCO3 <=> CaO + CO2) is increased by: A allowing the CO2 to escape, B increasing the heating time, C increasing the temperature, D reducing the pressure.
questions.answer: C - increasing the temperature
steps: Kc depends only on temperature, not on pressure, time or removal of CO2 from the system.
Decomposition of limestone is endothermic, so raising the temperature increases its equilibrium constant.
So option C is correct; options A, B and D do not change K.

questions.question: 10 mol N2 is heated with 30 mol H2 in a sealed container. At equilibrium 8.0 mol NH3 is present. What is the total amount of gas at equilibrium? Options: A 8.0, B 20, C 32, D 48.
questions.answer: C - 32 mol
steps: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3. 8.0 mol NH3 forms from 4.0 mol N2 and 12.0 mol H2.
Equilibrium N2 = 10 - 4.0 = 6.0 mol; H2 = 30 - 12.0 = 18.0 mol; NH3 = 8.0 mol.
Total gas = 6.0 + 18.0 + 8.0 = 32 mol, which is option C.

questions.question: What is the expression for the equilibrium constant Kp for N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g)?
steps: Products on the top: NH3 with coefficient 2.
Reactants on the bottom: N2 with coefficient 1 and H2 with coefficient 3.
So Kp = p(NH3)^2 / (p(N2) x p(H2)^3).

questions.question: Which change would increase the value of Kp for the ammonia equilibrium? Options: A decreasing the temperature, B decreasing the particle size of the catalyst, C increasing the total pressure, D increasing the concentration of hydrogen molecules.
questions.answer: A - decreasing the temperature
steps: Kp changes only with temperature; pressure, concentration and catalyst changes do not change Kp.
The forward reaction is exothermic, so lowering the temperature increases Kp.
So option A is correct.

questions.topic: Collisions That Do Not Give Products
questions.question: Some collisions between reactant molecules do not lead to products. What is the best explanation? Options: A reactant concentrations are too low, B the collisions do not have sufficient energy, C the reaction is at equilibrium, D the molecules do not collide in the correct ratio.
questions.answer: B - the collisions do not have sufficient energy
steps: Only collisions with energy at or above the activation energy lead to a reaction.
Many collisions have less than the activation energy and simply rebound.
So option B is the best explanation.

questions.question: For a reaction, Stotal = R ln K. Stotal for a reaction is negative. Which statement is true? Options: A the value of K is less than 1, B the value of K is greater than 1, C the value of K is negative, D the position of equilibrium lies to the right.
questions.answer: A - the value of K is less than 1
steps: Stotal = R ln K, so ln K has the same sign as Stotal.
Stotal is negative, so ln K is negative.
ln K < 0 means K < 1, so option A is true; the equilibrium lies to the left, so D is false.

questions.question: Ammonia is produced using an iron catalyst. Which statement about the catalyst is NOT correct? Options: A it lowers the activation energy, B it has no effect on the equilibrium constant, C it alters the enthalpy change of the reaction, D it reduces the energy cost of the reaction.
questions.answer: C - it alters the enthalpy change of the reaction
steps: A catalyst lowers the activation energy, so A is correct.
A catalyst does not change the equilibrium constant, so B is correct.
A catalyst does not change the enthalpy change of the reaction, so C is the incorrect statement.
Option D is a reasonable description, since a lower activation energy reduces the energy needed to run the process.

questions.question: Which conditions favour the highest percentage of ammonia in an equilibrium mixture from identical amounts of N2 and H2? Options: A 400 K and 200 kPa, B 400 K and 200 atm, C 400 C and 200 kPa, D 400 C and 200 atm.
questions.answer: B - 400 K and 200 atm
steps: The Haber reaction is exothermic, so a lower temperature favours the yield; 400 K is lower than 400 C (673 K).
Gas moles fall from 4 to 2, so a high pressure favours ammonia; 200 atm is much higher than 200 kPa (about 2 atm).
So the combination of 400 K and 200 atm gives the highest ammonia percentage, option B.

questions.question: Which statement about the equilibrium 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g) is correct? Options: A increasing pressure increases Kp, B decreasing pressure decreases the equilibrium yield of SO3, C adding a catalyst increases the equilibrium yield of SO3, D adding a catalyst increases Kp.
questions.answer: B - decreasing the pressure decreases the equilibrium yield of SO3
steps: Left side has 3 mol of gas and the right side has 2 mol.
Decreasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with more gas moles, which is the left (SO2 and O2).
So the equilibrium yield of SO3 falls, so B is correct.
Pressure and catalysts do not change Kp, so A and D are wrong, and a catalyst does not change the yield, so C is wrong.

questions.topic: Relationship Between K And Total Entropy
questions.question: What is the relationship between the equilibrium constant K and Stotal? Options: A Stotal = R ln K, B ln Stotal = RK, C Stotal = R log K, D log Stotal = RK.
questions.answer: A - Stotal = R ln K
steps: At equilibrium deltaG = 0 and deltaG = -RT ln K.
Stotal = -deltaG / T = R ln K.
So option A is correct.

questions.question: Using Kp = 4.0 x 10^24 atm-1 at 25 C for the equilibrium 2SO2 + O2 <=> 2SO3 (Equation 1), with R = 0.082 dm3 atm mol-1 K-1 and n = moles of product minus moles of reactants, calculate Kc. Options: A 1.64 x 10^23, B 1.95 x 10^24, C 8.20 x 10^24, D 9.77 x 10^25.
steps: For Equation 1: n = 2 - 3 = -1 (moles of product minus moles of reactant).
Kp = Kc (RT)^n, so Kc = Kp / (RT)^n = Kp x RT for n = -1.
Kc = 4.0 x 10^24 x 24.4 = 9.77 x 10^25, which is option D.

questions.topic: Pressure Effect On Colour Of Iodine Equilibrium
questions.question: The equilibrium H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g) is shown. What is the effect of an increase in pressure on the appearance of the equilibrium mixture? Options: A no change, B the mixture becomes more purple, C the mixture becomes more brown, D the mixture becomes less brown.
questions.answer: B - the mixture becomes more purple
steps: There are 2 mol of gas on each side, so pressure does not shift the equilibrium position.
Compressing the gas increases the concentration of all species, including I2.
Iodine vapour is purple, so the mixture becomes more intensely purple even though the equilibrium position does not change.

questions.topic: Change That Increases Kp For Haber Process
questions.question: For the Haber process with Kp = 6.76 x 10^5 atm-2 at 298 K, which change(s) will increase Kp? Options: A increase in pressure only, B decrease in temperature only, C increase in pressure and increase in temperature, D no change in pressure or temperature will affect Kp.
questions.answer: B - a decrease in temperature only
steps: Kp depends only on temperature, so pressure changes do not affect it (A is wrong).
The Haber reaction is exothermic, so lowering the temperature shifts equilibrium right and increases Kp.
So option B is correct.

questions.topic: Shift In Equilibrium From Increase In Kp
questions.question: For the equilibrium between NO2 and N2O4, Kp increases from 0.115 atm to 3.89 atm after a change in conditions. What can be deduced about the position of equilibrium? Options: A shifted towards products, B shifted towards reactants, C unchanged, D almost complete conversion of reactants into products.
questions.answer: A - the equilibrium position has shifted towards the products
steps: Kp is a measure of the position of equilibrium: a larger Kp means more products relative to reactants.
Kp increased from 0.115 atm to 3.89 atm, so the ratio of products to reactants increased.
The equilibrium has therefore shifted towards the products, option A.
Option D is not justified because 3.89 atm does not indicate almost complete conversion.

questions.question: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant Kc for 2NOCl(g) <=> 2NO(g) + Cl2(g).
questions.answer: Kc = [NO]^2 [Cl2] / [NOCl]^2
steps: Products on the top: NO with coefficient 2, Cl2 with coefficient 1.
Reactant on the bottom: NOCl with coefficient 2.
So Kc = [NO]^2 [Cl2] / [NOCl]^2.

questions.question: 0.250 mol NOCl in a 500 cm3 sealed container is heated to 200 C; at equilibrium there is 0.016 mol Cl2. Complete the table of equilibrium amounts or concentrations for NOCl, NO and Cl2 using the equilibrium equation and data.
questions.answer: Equilibrium: NOCl 0.218 mol (0.436 mol dm-3); NO 0.032 mol (0.064 mol dm-3); Cl2 0.016 mol (0.032 mol dm-3)
steps: Cl2 formed = 0.016 mol, so NOCl used = 2 x 0.016 = 0.032 mol and NO formed = 0.032 mol.
Equilibrium NOCl = 0.250 - 0.032 = 0.218 mol.
Volume = 0.500 dm3, so concentrations are: NOCl = 0.436, NO = 0.064, Cl2 = 0.032 mol dm-3.

questions.topic: Nature Of Reaction From Temperature Effect On Kc
questions.question: When the temperature is reduced, Kc becomes smaller. Explain what can be deduced about the nature of the reaction.
questions.answer: The forward reaction is endothermic, since lowering the temperature reduces Kc, so the equilibrium shifts to the reverse (exothermic) direction
steps: Kc decreases when temperature decreases, so the equilibrium shifts towards reactants on cooling.
The shift to the reactants is the exothermic direction for the reverse reaction.
So the reverse reaction is exothermic and the forward reaction is endothermic (deltaH positive).
